2. Purpose

This checklist shall be conducted by competent persons whilst adhering to the provisions of all relevant laws and regulations.

After completion of all visual inspections from the checklist, the service provider must perform the required maintenance tasks on the relevant components.

The extent of inspection for each item is indicated as follows:

Incident Report – Three Star Method

Site / Plant

Time of incident

Reported by

1. What happened? (Facts and observations)

Provide a clear and factual account of the incident. Describe the time, date and location; who was involved; what actions or events occurred leading to the incident; and any immediate impact or outcomes (e.g. injuries, system failures, downtime). Focus on objective details without assigning blame.

Example: “On January 12, 2025, at 2:00 PM, a circuit breaker in Solar Plant B tripped, causing a temporary power outage in Sector 3. The technician on-site reported a burning smell before the trip occurred. The outage lasted for 2 hours, affecting energy supply to nearby facilities.”

2. Why did it happen? (Root cause analysis)

Explore the underlying reasons and contributing factors. Use tools like the 5 Whys or a Fishbone diagram to identify root causes. Address technical failures (e.g. equipment malfunction, design flaw), human factors (e.g. lack of training, miscommunication) and environmental conditions (e.g. weather, external disruptions).

Example: “The circuit breaker tripped due to overheating caused by a loose connection in the panel. Routine inspections had not identified the issue due to insufficient thermal imaging during maintenance checks.”

3. How can it be prevented? (Actionable recommendations)

Propose corrective and preventive measures. Focus on immediate actions (e.g. repair or replacement of faulty equipment), long-term solutions (e.g. updated training programmes, better monitoring systems) and continuous-improvement initiatives (e.g. scheduled audits, upgraded technology).

Example: “Repair loose connections and replace damaged components in the panel. Update maintenance protocols to include thermal imaging inspections. Train staff on identifying early signs of electrical stress.”

Sungrow Handover Document

Customer

Plant / site name

Prepared by

Your system is live!

Congratulations, your solar system is live!

You now have access to a reliable power supply that is not harmful to the environment.

This document provides monitoring and support information. But don’t hesitate to reach out if any questions remain!

We hope you’ve enjoyed your hassle-free experience thus far and we’ll be in touch whenever we pick up a problem or for our annual maintenance trip.

Section 1. Real-Time Monitoring

This section gives you a run-down on the monitoring software iSolarCloud. If you don’t feel like monitoring your system, don’t worry – we will do it daily in any case.

Step 1. Create an account

  • Go to https://www.isolarcloud.com/ on your web browser

  • Select “Register”

  • Select “International Server”

  • Select “End User”

  • Enter your e-mail address

  • Select “Send Verification Code”

  • You will receive an e-mail from iSolarCloud with the activation code

  • Enter the verification code provided in the e-mail

  • Enter your preferred password

  • Select South Africa

  • Select time zone UTC+2:00 Harare, Pretoria

  • Accept the privacy policy

  • Click “Register”

  • Registration was successful – proceed to login

Step 2. Access your account

  • Make sure “International Server” is selected

  • Enter your login details

  • Click “Login”

  • Select “Agree”

  • Click on your plant’s name to open the dashboard

  • If you have multiple projects with us, you will see multiple plants here

Step 3. Monitor your plant

  • The dashboard shows the solar system’s production, the grid consumption and the total customer consumption

The meaning of the different icons: solar production, consumption from the grid and total consumption.

Self-consumption

  • 100% means all power is self-consumed (none has been pushed into the grid)

  • The revenue is calculated as the savings per kWh times the daily production

  • Today’s yield is today’s solar production

Statistics

  • Real-time power displays the current production from the solar system

  • Current month’s yield is the cumulative production for the current month

  • Total yield displays the system’s production over its full life

  • Statistics can be viewed on a day / month / year and total level

  • The load graph displays 1) solar production (self-sufficient) as well as 2) energy purchased from the grid

Graphs

  • The load displays customer demand. The load is equal to the grid power when solar is not available (e.g. at night)

  • PV equals the solar power. It is available 6 AM – 6 PM and strongest 10 AM – 2 PM

  • Grid equals the municipal or Eskom supply

  • Data can be exported in the required format

Carbon footprint

  • Carbon dioxide emission reduction, standard coal saving and equivalent tree-planting index data are calculated based on the total yield of the plant

  • If you are liable for carbon tax, this statistic can be used by your accountant

Prefer to use the iSolarCloud app instead?

  • Apple: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/isolarcloud-yun-ying/id1050077439

  • Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.isolarcloud.manager

  • Switch to the international server and log in with the same login details

Section 2. Safety Features

In most cases the system will protect itself, but in case of emergency, follow these steps. If you need to switch off or reboot the system (no emergency), you also follow the steps below.

Switching off the system

  1. Isolate the PV DB main breaker

  2. Switch the PV isolator on the inverter to the OFF position

Restarting the system

  1. Switch the PV isolator on the inverter (back) to the ON position

  2. Switch on (pull up) the PV DB main breaker

Checking whether the system is communicating with the monitoring software

  1. “Run” should be green (tells you whether the system is operating)

  2. “WLAN” should be blue (tells you whether there is communication)

In the event of a fire

Extinguish the fire with a CO2 or dry powder extinguisher. Sosimple has provided you with a suitable extinguisher, located inside the inverter room. NEVER try to put out a fire on electrical equipment with water, foam or wet chemical extinguishers.

Section 3. Billing Meter

Monitoring versus billing

We’ve shown you in detail which software we use to monitor your plant. We do this on a daily basis, in order to schedule maintenance if and when needed.

The monitoring is based on inverter production. We’re not allowed to bill you based on this information.

For billing purposes, we have installed a certified billing meter next to your inverter. This smart meter can be read remotely. This information is used to send you our monthly invoice.

The monitoring data can vary ±5% from the billing meter. The billing meter is regarded as the single measure of truth.

Do let us know if you either require access to the billing meter or would like a copy of the calibration certificate.

Section 4. Sosimple Support

For technical enquiries, our support team can be reached via:

  • E: support@sosimpleenergy.co.za

  • T: 072 970 3254

For any other queries, your account manager can be reached via:

  • E: liana.braxton@sosimpleenergy.co.za

  • T: 067 347 1744

Section 1. Real-Time Monitoring

This section gives you a run-down on the monitoring software MyPower24. If you don’t feel like monitoring your system, don’t worry – we will do it daily in any case.

Step 1. Create an account

  • An e-mail invitation will be sent from “mypower24@solarmd.co.za”

  • Click on the “Accept Invitation” link in the e-mail. It will redirect you to your web browser and open the MyPower24 login page

  1. Click on the “Create new Account” button

  2. Fill in your details

  3. Click on “Create Account”

Step 2. Access your account

  • Log in to your account by entering your username and password and clicking the “Sign in” button

  • Click on the “Accept” button on the window that opens after you have signed in

  • The site is now successfully added to your account!

Step 3. Monitor your plant

  • The dashboard on the MyPower24 login shows the solar system’s production, the power fed from the grid, the battery levels and the total customer consumption

  • The bottom of the dashboard shows environmental benefits, financial benefits and energy usage

The meaning of the different symbols on the dashboard:

  • Solar production: daily production and total production

  • Consumption from the grid

  • Battery size, percentage and consumption

  • Load consumption

Environmental benefits

  • Water saved, carbon dioxide reduction and trips with an electric car are calculated based on the total yield of the plant

  • If you are liable for carbon tax, this statistic can be used by your accountant

  • The menu on the left of the MyPower24 homepage gives access to different monitoring elements such as graphs, connected devices and the system and faults

  • Click on the “My charts” drop-down menu to access various graphs of the plant

Graphs: power simple graph

Graphs: power graph

Graphs: energy graph

Prefer to use the MyPower24 app instead?

  • Apple: https://apps.apple.com/za/app/mypower24/id6443918134

  • Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.solarmd.mypower24&hl=en_US

Section 2. Safety Features

In most cases the system will protect itself, but in case of emergency, follow these steps. If you need to switch off or reboot the system (no emergency), you also follow the steps below.

Grid-tied inverter safety procedure – isolating

  1. Isolate the PV DB main breaker by pushing the switch down

  2. Switch the PV isolator on the Sungrow inverter to the “OFF” position

  1. Disconnect the grid-tied inverter on Bypass 500 by pushing the “INV” breaker switch down

Grid-tied inverter safety procedure – restarting the PV system

  1. Switch the PV isolator on the Sungrow inverter (back) to the “ON” position

  2. Switch on (pull up) the PV DB main breaker

  1. Switch on the grid-tied inverter on Bypass 500 by pulling the “INV” breaker switch up

PV safety procedure – isolating PV

  • If there is a fault on any string, strings can be isolated in the DB next to the panels

  • Switch the DC isolator to the “OFF” position. Contact Sosimple Support before switching the string on

Atess PCS safety procedure: fault – isolating the battery inverter

  1. If a fault occurs, press “emergency stop” and contact Sosimple Support

  2. Disconnect the AC breaker and battery breaker inside the PCS 500

  1. Isolate the batteries by turning the BMU isolator to the off position

  1. Switch on the “Bypass” breaker and disconnect all other breakers. The system will be switched on after Sosimple Support has attended to the fault

Atess PCS safety procedure: switching off the inverter

  • Click the “ON/OFF” button on the homepage to open the “ON/OFF” interface

  • Click the “OFF” button on the “ON/OFF” interface to switch off the inverter

  • Turn the “ON/OFF” knob to the “off” position

Atess PCS safety procedure: switching on the inverter

  • Turn the “ON/OFF” knob to the “on” position

  • Click the “ON” button on the “ON/OFF” interface

Checking whether the system is communicating with the monitoring software

  1. “Connection LED” should be green

  2. “System LED” should be green

  3. “RS485-1” LED should be green

  4. “RS485-2” LED should be green

If any LEDs are off or red, please contact Sosimple Support.

In the event of a fire on electrical equipment

Extinguish the fire with a CO2 or dry powder extinguisher. Sosimple has provided you with a suitable extinguisher, located inside the inverter room. NEVER try to put out a fire on electrical equipment with water, foam or wet chemical extinguishers.

In the event of a fire on batteries

Extinguish the fire with a Lith-Ex fire extinguisher. Sosimple has provided you with a suitable extinguisher, located inside the inverter room. NEVER try to put out a fire on batteries with water, foam or wet chemical extinguishers.
